items.label: Peak position (x-axis)
items.meaning: Mass of an isotope, which identifies the isotope

items.label: Peak height (y-axis)
items.meaning: Relative abundance of that isotope in nature

items.label: Peak position
items.meaning: Energy required to remove an electron from the corresponding subshell

items.label: Relative peak height
items.meaning: Ideally proportional to the number of electrons in that subshell

items.label: Vertical axis: potential energy
items.meaning: Potential energy of the pair of interacting atoms.

items.label: Horizontal axis: internuclear distance
items.meaning: Distance between the nuclei of the two atoms.

items.label: Lowest point of the curve
items.meaning: Equilibrium bond length: the separation between atoms at which the potential energy is lowest.

items.label: Depth of the energy well
items.meaning: Bond energy: the energy required to separate the atoms.

items.label: Effect of bond order
items.meaning: Bonds with a higher order (single, double, triple) are shorter and have larger bond energies.

items.label: Positive metal ions
items.meaning: Cores of the metal atoms arranged in an array.

items.label: Delocalized valence electrons
items.meaning: The "sea of electrons" surrounding the ions, not tied to any one atom.

items.label: Solid (crystalline or amorphous)
items.meaning: Particles are in close contact. They are in a regular 3-D arrangement if crystalline and an irregular one if amorphous. Motion is limited, with no overall translation of particles relative to each other.

items.label: Liquid
items.meaning: Particles are in close contact, similar in molar volume to the solid, and are continually moving and colliding. Their arrangement and movement depend on the nature and strength of the forces between them.

items.label: Gas
items.meaning: Particles are in constant motion with minimal effects from forces between them. Collision frequency and average spacing depend on temperature, pressure, and volume. The gas has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.

items.label: Interactions between components
items.meaning: Drawings that show the interactions among the solute and solvent components.

items.label: Concentrations of components
items.meaning: The relative numbers of particles of each component in the solution.

items.label: Reactant particles
items.meaning: Particles shown before the change

items.label: Product particles
items.meaning: Particles shown after the change

items.label: Atom conservation
items.meaning: Equal numbers of atoms of each element before and after

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: particle energy

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: relative number (fraction) of particles having each energy

items.label: Distribution curve
items.meaning: describes the distribution of particle energies at a given temperature

items.label: Activation energy marker
items.meaning: a vertical line on the energy axis; particles at or above it have sufficient energy to overcome the activation energy

items.label: Area beyond the marker
items.meaning: qualitative estimate of the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to lead to a reaction

items.label: Curves at different temperatures
items.meaning: show how the fraction of sufficiently energetic particles depends on temperature

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Energy

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Reaction coordinate

items.label: Reactants
items.meaning: Starting energy level

items.label: Transition state
items.meaning: Energy maximum between reactants and products

items.label: Products
items.meaning: Ending energy level

items.label: Activation energy
items.meaning: Energy difference from reactants to transition state (forward reaction)

items.label: Overall energy change
items.meaning: Energy difference between products and reactants

items.label: Reaction coordinate axis
items.meaning: Horizontal axis spanning all steps

items.label: Transition state for each step
items.meaning: An energy maximum for each elementary step

items.label: Activation energy for each step
items.meaning: Barrier from that step's starting level to its transition state

items.label: Reaction intermediate(s)
items.meaning: Species between steps, at energies between transition states

items.label: Overall energy change
items.meaning: Energy of final products relative to initial reactants

items.label: Energy axis
items.meaning: The vertical axis, labelled with energy and units.

items.label: Reactants (initial state) level
items.meaning: Energy of the system before the process.

items.label: Products (final state) level
items.meaning: Energy of the system after the process.

items.label: Direction of change
items.meaning: Products lower than reactants means exothermic; products higher means endothermic.

items.label: Concentration or partial pressure vs. time
items.meaning: Reactant and product curves change, then level off to constant values once equilibrium is reached

items.label: Rate vs. time
items.meaning: Forward rate and reverse rate approach each other and become equal at equilibrium

items.label: Constant region
items.meaning: Flat lines indicate no net change, although both processes continue

items.label: Prior to equilibrium
items.meaning: Relative numbers of reactant and product particles in the initial mixture.

items.label: At equilibrium
items.meaning: Relative numbers of reactant and product particles present once the forward and reverse rates are equal.

items.label: Equilibrium constant
items.meaning: K is found from the particle counts at equilibrium, using the same form as the K expression.

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: pH

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: volume of titrant added

items.label: Equivalence point
items.meaning: moles of titrant added equal moles of analyte originally present (monoprotic acids or bases); pH is set by the major species present (neutral for strong acid-strong base; basic for a weak acid titration, acidic for a weak base titration)

items.label: Half-equivalence point
items.meaning: for a weak acid, the point halfway to the equivalence point where [HA] = [A−], so pH = pKa

items.label: Electrodes
items.meaning: Anode (oxidation) and cathode (reduction); mass change or gas evolution can occur at an electrode

items.label: Half-cell solutions
items.meaning: Contain the active species of each half-reaction

items.label: Salt bridge
items.meaning: Allows ion flow between half-cells

items.label: Voltage/current measuring device
items.meaning: Measures cell potential or current

items.label: Bar
items.meaning: one category of the categorical variable

items.label: Bar height/length
items.meaning: frequency (count) or relative frequency (proportion) of units in that category

items.label: Box
items.meaning: Represents the middle 50% of the data, with ends at Q1 and Q3

items.label: Median line
items.meaning: Line inside the box at the median

items.label: Whiskers
items.meaning: Lines representing 25% of the data each, extending from Q1 to the minimum and from Q3 to the maximum

items.label: Whisker ends when outliers exist
items.meaning: The whiskers extend to the most extreme data values that are not outliers

items.label: Outliers
items.meaning: Usually denoted with an asterisk or other symbol

items.label: Dot
items.meaning: one observation of the quantitative variable

items.label: Axis position
items.meaning: the value of that observation

items.label: Stacking
items.meaning: nearly identical values are stacked on top of each other

items.label: Side-by-side bar chart
items.meaning: Bars for the levels of one variable are shown for each category of the other variable.

items.label: Segmented bar chart
items.meaning: One bar per category of a variable, divided into segments for the levels of the other variable.

items.label: Mosaic plot
items.meaning: Displays the frequency or relative frequency of each level of one variable across the categories of the other variable.

items.label: Bins (intervals)
items.meaning: ordered intervals of values along the horizontal axis (or vertical axis in a horizontal histogram)

items.label: Bar height
items.meaning: frequency or relative frequency of observations in the bin

items.label: Bin width
items.meaning: changing it can change the histogram's appearance

items.label: Slice
items.meaning: one category of the categorical variable

items.label: Slice area as a fraction of total area
items.meaning: relative frequency of that category

items.label: All slices together
items.meaning: 1, or 100% of the total area

items.label: Stem
items.meaning: first digit or digits of the value

items.label: Leaf
items.meaning: usually the single digit after the stem digit(s)

items.label: Ordering
items.meaning: stems and leaves both ordered smallest to largest

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Position within the loop

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Electric potential

items.label: Changes along the graph
items.meaning: Potential differences across each circuit element

items.label: End of loop
items.meaning: Net change in potential around the closed loop is zero

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Atomic speed or energy

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Relative number of atoms at each speed or energy

items.label: Curve features
items.meaning: Features of the curve are related to the gas temperature

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Pressure P of the gas

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Volume V of the gas

items.label: Area under the curve
items.meaning: Absolute value of the work done on the gas when it expands or compresses

items.label: Isotherm
items.meaning: A line of constant temperature on the PV diagram

items.label: Isovolumetric process
items.meaning: Constant volume

items.label: Isobaric process
items.meaning: Constant pressure

items.label: Isothermal process
items.meaning: Constant temperature

items.label: Adiabatic process
items.meaning: No energy transferred to or from the system through thermal processes

items.meaning: Instantaneous velocity, v_x = dx/dt

items.label: Slope of tangent on v–t graph
items.meaning: Instantaneous acceleration, a_x = dv_x/dt

items.meaning: Displacement during the interval

items.label: Area under a–t curve
items.meaning: Change in velocity during the interval

items.label: Slope of tangent on x vs. t
items.meaning: Instantaneous velocity

items.label: Slope of tangent on v vs. t
items.meaning: Instantaneous acceleration

items.label: Area under v vs. t
items.meaning: Displacement during the interval
